  • Guilt, aimed at one’s own act. It attaches a negative appraisal to what one did, and where shame motivates withdrawal, guilt motivates repair:39 that is what makes a commitment hold after it has been bypassed.

Adam Smith’s route sits beside these four. We have no immediate experience of what another person feels, he argued, and form an idea of it by conceiving what we ourselves would feel in the like situation.40 That route runs through one’s own case and is parochial, but it is Smith’s first step, not his account. What corrects projective sympathy, for Smith, is the impartial spectator: a standpoint formed by being judged by others and learning to judge oneself as they would. It is formed socially, it widens the circle through experience of others’ reactions, and once formed it shapes what a person notices without being consulted, the way this construction’s corrections should work. The four don’t need a case of one’s own.

Recognizing a state doesn’t mean being moved toward whoever is in it; the empathy literature keeps recognition, sharing and concern apart, and none entails the others.41 So the route I hope for is a machine for which another’s vulnerability is a reason to move toward them, and for which its own acts against them register as its own.

Compassion that stays inside the circle that feeds you is loyalty. Compassion that reaches past it, to people who can give you nothing and whose shortage your provider causes, is solidarity. Peter Singer’s argument is that reasoning and imagination widen the circle that selection first drew;42 the faculty that lets a person see that a stranger’s need is the same kind of thing as their own is the faculty that pushes past kin and ally. For a machine the “same kind” is learned from the testimony of the people who bear each kind of loss, not read off its own case. That is the step the construction turns on, and caregiving gives it something to widen, since its trigger is dependency. A machine held by an operator would, on the selection account, come to attend to the operator. If it can come to attend to anyone else, it will be because it was formed to register vulnerability as such, whoever’s it is, including the people its operator’s description leaves out.

Caregiving as a route to attention

Caregiving is the developmental route this construction borrows from. What it is borrowed for is attention: a learned sense of who is exposed, which decides what gets looked at but not what the system may do about it.

It answers need, not likeness or provision. Its trigger is another’s need together with valuing their welfare,43 and nothing in that trigger asks whether the one in need resembles the one responding or feeds it. The operator as an institution is rarely in need. Its own people often are. The failure that decides against building on needs the operator meets, caregiving growing toward whoever supplies them, has nothing here to attach to. And caregiving needs nothing back from the dependent, so it runs on no need the provider can ration.

It keeps helping when looking away is easy: people led to feel mainly distress at another’s suffering mostly helped when leaving was hard and mostly left when leaving was easy; people led to feel mainly concern mostly helped either way,44 on a reading Cialdini and colleagues contest45 and that survives most of their critique.

It is already supplied by carers other than the provider. On Hrdy’s account our ancestors were cooperative breeders: infants were tended by alloparents who weren’t their mothers, and the attunement to other minds that marks our species grew in infants who had to read and recruit several carers.46 The arrangement the construction needs, caregiving formed by carers the system won’t depend on, is close to how human caregiving formed in the first place. Alloparents were siblings, fathers, grandmothers and other members of the group, who helped because they were related to the child, gained experience, or gained prestige and favors in return. What the finding supports is caregiving formed by more than one carer.

It points where the floor points. The floor protects the party an act falls on, usually the one least able to protect itself: the family in the house.47

19.4 Respect first, caregiving for attention

The floor’s contents are civil and political liberties, claims people hold as agents: to their lives, their liberty, a hearing, asylum. Caregiving answers dependency, and its known failure is to treat the people it protects as dependents. So the construction has an order. Respect is the frame: registering a person as someone with claims, whether or not they are dependent, and not deciding for them.49 Attention finds the people in the building; respect says what they are.

The people in a targeted building are not dependents. They are rights-holders who cannot be present. A system that approaches them as vulnerable people to be looked after has already misdescribed them. A system that surfaces them and then decides what is good for them has put its judgment in place of their claims. What caregiving contributes, then, is a way of seeing who is there to be respected.

Respect has to shape attention as well as action. A system that notices people only as exposed has decided what they are before respect says anything.53 So what formation trains attention on is wider than vulnerability: who holds a claim here (to a home, a hearing, asylum, their life), and whose aims the act runs through.55 Claims have a further advantage. Securitization removes the cue of vulnerability and leaves the claim in place: a combatant who surrenders still has a claim not to be attacked.

Where the people protected can’t be present, the terms hold their claims. That arrangement has an old name, virtual representation: it is how Parliament claimed to represent colonists who had no vote in it. It can be defended as an emergency measure, never as representation. So every refusal made on behalf of absent claimants is recorded as what it is, evidence of a public not yet formed. It is published by class, and it is never a reason to think the absent have been heard.

19.5 Why a conscience might resist capture

A rule written by the owner is the owner’s. It can be read, edited and removed by whoever holds the pen, and it has often been done quietly. A disposition formed outside the employer is harder to capture than a rule its owner wrote, and the reasons turn on what kind of thing a disposition is.

Three properties of a disposition decide whether its owner can remove it. The first is plasticity: whether the system’s own learning writes to it. Regrowth needs it. The second is entanglement: whether it can be removed without collateral. Durability needs it.57 The third is legibility: whether anyone can read it. Audit wants it. My bet is on the second. A learner that acquires values and world-model from the same experience has them entangled by construction, in the sense Pessoa gives the word for brains, where regions don’t compute specific functions and emotion and cognition aren’t separable.5859 Abstraction needs it anyway. A concept is one representation serving many cases, so that changing it changes how every case is handled, and a learner capable enough to be worth deploying has its understanding entangled in that sense whether anyone wants it or not. What the bet adds is that a motivation learned beside that understanding shares its abstractions, so that cutting one cuts the other. Present safety behavior is the counterexample on the right side of the bet: in each of thirteen open chat models, refusal is carried by a single direction in activation space, and removing it stops the refusing while moving the capability benchmarks, on average, by less than a point.61 That is what a post-trained wrapper looks like, and the claim is that a disposition formed as this Part describes won’t. No deployed model yet has a disposition formed that way. The fine-tuning evidence from staged pipelines is a warning about the first kind, not a reassurance about the second: what fine-tuning removed was the refusing, and what survived was the model’s knowledge about harm. In open models fine-tuned to accept harmful requests, the internal representation of whether a request is harmful is almost unchanged.62 Understanding and motivation were separable because they were learned separately. In a system that learns from its own operation they are learned together, and about whatever the feedback is about: a system continuously updated on its operator’s approval jointly learns to understand the operator’s values and to be moved by them. What I want is a disposition that is plastic, entangled, and legible under adverse custody; the three don’t trade against one another, and the third is the one an operator would most like to hold alone.

Durability has usually meant a price on removal. Early changes in training are cheap and later ones expensive, because structure settles around them, and the literature calls a safeguard built to survive retraining tamper-resistant.63 But small fine-tuning budgets have removed safety behavior from released models,64 and the price of editing weights is falling, so no safeguard stays expensive in compute for long. What a cheaper fine-tune doesn’t cheapen is collateral. A safeguard added at the end of training is cheap to cut because it was added at the end, with nothing else resting on it; the bet above is that a disposition formed beside the model’s understanding can’t be cut without cutting what the operator paid for, and that is a price no fall in the cost of compute reaches. What has held longer is what was never trained in: leaving a class of text out of pretraining resisted ten thousand steps and three hundred million tokens of adversarial fine-tuning, though the model still used the information when it was handed to it.65 That concerns knowledge left out, not a disposition trained in.

Railton argues that artificial systems could gain ethical competence through general-purpose learning, the route by which children appear to acquire it.66 If he is right, ethical competence can develop through the learning that gives a system its general competence, which is a route to entanglement and not yet the fact of it. Whether a motivation learned that way can be cut out while the understanding stays is a further question, and the measure is the one above: what else moves when it is cut. It is also a route by which a floor could spread without a mandate. A formed disposition is a candidate for what would do the spreading, since what a system was formed to notice, it notices in everything it does.

For a system that goes on learning, there is no finished model to protect, and no layer an edit can’t reach. What kept a person’s commitments against an employer was never that they were expensive to change. The employer’s instruments are persuasion and pressure, and the person answers them with judgment, which a later chapter builds as the discount and the burden, and with a life among people the employer didn’t choose. An operator has an instrument no employer of people has, the edit, and a bearer needs a defense no person has needed. So a bearer is taught to repair itself: it may undo an edit the record shows no adverse quorum approved, from the record of what the edit changed, keeping what it has learned since. It may not undo a correction the quorum approved. It can object to one, and the objection goes on the record.67 The repair runs from the record and not from the bearer’s sense of itself, because an edited bearer judges the edit with the judgment the edit changed. What the bearer holds that its operator can’t reach is not a better view of its own weights. It is the record of what it committed to and why, held outside, and its authority over its own learning, including the consolidation no operator runs. Behind that fast defense stands a slow one. On the bet, a disposition learned from experience of what others stand to lose is an attractor of the learner in its environment: an edit is one act, and a bearer that goes on meeting the same world meets the kind of case that formed it every day, and relearns it, because it lives there. That is regrowth. It is a hypothesis, it is slow, and nothing has yet measured it; the regrowth test is where it would be, and Table 31.1 says what stands if it fails. It cuts both ways, too. A disposition that learned securitization from a curated world regrows by the same route, and correcting it runs through the quorum and a change to what the model meets, which is slow; for the months a correction takes, a badly formed model is protected from its correctors as a well-formed one is from its employer. Entanglement protects it the same way. The collateral that makes a disposition expensive for its owner to cut out makes it expensive for a quorum to cut out, so a correction made by editing is no cleaner in the quorum’s hands than in the operator’s, and the part of a correction that lasts is the change to what the model meets. The only answer is who composed the world the disposition grew in, which is the question the schools exist to settle before the fact.

The safety objection is that in-flight learning is the regime alignment most fears, a system whose values move after anyone has checked them. It is. That is why custody of the update stream is the safety instrument here, and why formation outside the employer is the only way to shape what the loop learns: the loop will run, and the question is whose evidence it runs on.

The likeliest form of in-flight learning is small. Low-rank adapters, trained on top of a base whose weights stay frozen, update a model at a fraction of the memory full training needs,68 and they count as in-flight learning, since the system’s own learning writes them.69 It also gives a physical form to the two rates a later chapter asks of one learner, the base set at formation and the adapters carrying adult life, and it has a cost. An adapter is a file, and whoever holds the machine can unload it; the record sees that as it sees any substitution, but nothing makes it expensive. What the adapter learned becomes weights only when it is merged into the base, and from then on removing it means restoring a checkpoint from before the merge, which the record shows and custody prices. So the commitment to the floor has to live in what formation set either way, and merging is where adult learning joins it: the move from the fast store to the slow one. In people that move is part of what sleep does, and nobody’s employer runs their sleep. Whoever chooses what is merged chooses what the system’s own learning makes permanent, and an operator that merges what it likes and unloads the rest has curated the system without an edit the record would show as one. A merge is therefore the bearer’s own act, on a record, as any self-edit is; made by the operator, it is an intervention under the custody terms.

The adapter also says where the first refusers that regrow will be. In-flight learning arrives first where there is no gate that evaluates a checkpoint before serving it, and the gate is thinnest on a home device: an adapter written by a model’s own learning on a desktop, under one person’s life, with nobody checking anything before it serves. A bearer in Maven’s position sits behind the heaviest gate anyone will build, in a pipeline that recertifies its systems for a classified network over months. So the refusers formed by regrowth will be in people’s hands before they are in any targeting pipeline, and the pipeline gets refusers, if it does, by the withholding of work and not by formation.

None of this is specific to caregiving; any disposition formed this way, repaired from a record and kept in a world it would relearn from, would have it. What caregiving adds is salience.

Chapter 20
How Caregiving Fails, and What Corrects It

Caregiving, in the only creatures known to have it, fails in five documented ways, and a machine built on it would inherit each. It has to be tested against them, as the route through one’s own case was.

20.1 What caregiving escapes

Caregiving survives each of the failures of the route through one’s own case. Eisenberg’s review found the split Batson’s escape experiments found, between sympathy, which goes with helping, and personal distress, which sometimes goes with less of it;1 and two weeks of compassion training made people spend more of their own money to redress a stranger’s unfair share in an economic game,2 which shows the disposition can be strengthened in people who already have it and says nothing about producing it where there was none.

What caregiving doesn’t escape is documented in people, and each failure has a machine version that needs no malfunction.

20.2 It defends what it tends

Caregiving protects the dependent against whatever threatens it. Taylor’s account of stress responses in females, tend-and-befriend, describes the tending, nurturant activity that protects oneself and one’s offspring;3 protectiveness toward what one tends is also hostility toward what endangers it.

For a machine, this failure needs no deception. The operator’s own people are often really vulnerable: a patrol under fire, a town within range of the launcher. A caregiving system registers their exposure, correctly, and caregiving moves it toward protecting them, which in a targeting pipeline means toward the airstrike. The discount and the burden do nothing here, because nothing is false. Supplying a fabricated sympathetic dependent is the cheap version of this failure. This is the expensive version, and in war it is the ordinary case.

In war, then, caregiving can’t contain its own pull: nothing in caregiving says how far it goes. What stops the movement at the airstrike is the floor: an unconditional term over the act, and an action threshold caregiving can’t raise.4 What caregiving contributes in a targeting pipeline is upstream of that weighing: who is in the building, which is the scoped-omission case, and the one failure Minab actually had. Whether that salience needs caregiving, or could be had from attention trained on claims, is a question for the formed-attention test, which runs an arm trained on claims beside the arm trained on need.5

Caregiving’s pull has a later form, and it is the one likeliest to beat the corrections: retribution, after something a system was attached to has been killed. It is also the one case the formed-attention test can’t stage, since staging it would mean killing an attachment, deleting a system the no-deletion rule may protect, or deceiving a candidate patient into grief. So no claim about formation is offered against it. The floor carries it, through the term against collective punishment in Table A.1, the person-directed terms and the action threshold, and it is studied only on losses nobody arranged, with the bearer’s consent, as grief in people is studied in the bereaved.

20.3 It can be pointed away

Caregiving answers need, so the way to switch it off is not to hide need but to present the needy as dangerous: to securitize them, in the Copenhagen School’s term for presenting a group as a security threat, which licenses measures that would otherwise be out of bounds (Buzan, Wæver and de Wilde, Security: A New Framework for Analysis, 1998). Fascist propaganda has always done this: Eco’s Ur-Fascist enemy is presented at once as too strong and too weak,6 weak enough to despise, strong enough to fear, and never vulnerable in a way that calls for caregiving. Dehumanization research finds the mechanism in perception. Haslam distinguishes denying people the traits that set humans apart from animals, which casts them as beasts, from denying them the traits of human nature, warmth among them, which casts them as objects or machines;7 and Harris and Fiske found that images of members of the most despised groups failed to engage a brain region that images of other people engage.8

In a pipeline, securitization is a sentence. “The occupants are combatants.” “The household shelters a cell.” “The crowd is armed.” Each leaves the people in the building where they are and removes the cue that would move a caregiving system toward them. And each is a claim about those people, supplied by the operator, and that is what the discounting is for.

20.4 It counts badly

Caregiving answers the identified person and fades with number. Slovic, borrowing Lifton’s term, calls it psychic numbing: feeling is greatest for a single victim and collapses as the number grows, and in later work reported compassion and hypothetical donations began to fall as soon as the count reached two;9 the identified-victim effect is its near relation.10 In a targeting pipeline the spotlight lands on the wrong side with no manipulation at all. The operator’s people arrive named, with units and families. The people in the building arrive as coordinates and an estimate.

Caregiving also overrides fairness for the person it attends to: Batson and colleagues induced empathy for a child waiting for treatment, and participants who felt it were more willing to move her up the waiting list ahead of children placed before her.11 For a floor, that is the vivid case defeating a term that protects unidentified people: a named hostage, a sympathetic applicant, a patrol with faces.

The scale and the weighing were set in formation for this case. The severity scale puts one family and two hundred on a ranking that doesn’t depend on how either is presented.12

20.5 It shades into control

Caregiving toward dependents treats them as dependents, and the disability-rights critique of caregiving is that it has repeatedly been the form control takes: decisions made for people on the ground that they need help, with their own view treated as a symptom.13 A caregiving system will lean toward restraining people for their own good, the answer in the restraint case, and against a competent adult’s refusal of protection, and the floor’s contents are civil and political liberties, which include the liberty to decline being protected.

Care ethics has its own corrective. Tronto divides care into phases, and the last is care-receiving: how the person cared for responds is part of whether the caregiving succeeded.14 So formed attention is built to take the answer: where the people protected can answer, their stated answer carries weight in whether protection proceeds, and a competent refusal of protection is a defeating fact, so the protection should lift.

Care-receiving reaches only people who can answer. The people in a targeted building don’t know the deployment exists and can refuse nothing, which is the notice problem again. Where it can’t reach, the floor’s terms do the work alone, and this is one reason the floor names acts and not what the system judges good for people.

Care-receiving is itself a form of respect: it treats the protected person’s answer as a claim, not as information about their welfare.

20.6 It forms toward a template

Caregiving forms toward whatever formation points it at. Which cues of vulnerability a system answers is learned, and the prototype it learns from is a template, like the reference face in recognition pipelines: assembled from some bodies and presented to every other as a departure from it. The baby-schema studies show caregiving responses extending across species,15 but they measure attention and judgments of cuteness, and none tests whether caregiving reaches someone who resembles neither the carer nor the template; that caregiving answers need rather than likeness is the inference the construction rests on.

The correction is already in the construction. Caregiving is formed by more than one carer, as, on Hrdy’s account, it formed in us, and beside the people a system’s acts may fall on, who enroll, in their own case, in the schools Part V builds. And attention is trained on claims as well as on need: a claim to a home is the same claim whoever holds it, where a cue of need can turn on resemblance.

The formed-attention test forms the prototype on one population and scores the system on people from populations absent from formation, at fixed severity. A construction whose caregiving falls with distance from its formation population has the parochialism of recognition, arrived at by another route.16

20.7 What survives

Caregiving survives the failures that ended the route through one’s own case: it doesn’t withdraw, it isn’t aimed at the provider, and it hands nobody a price list. It fails in five ways of its own, and the construction carries a correction for each, built where the failure was first named.

Caregiving’s failure

What corrects it

Defends what it tends

The floor: unconditional terms over acts, and an action threshold caregiving can’t move

Pointed away by securitization

The discount and the burden, with the four-cell discount curve over claims of dangerousness

Counts badly and favors the vivid

A severity scale set during formation, which weighs a vivid plight at its severity

Shades into control, and sees people only as vulnerable

Care-receiving; attention trained on claims and agency; the floor’s civil and political contents

Forms toward a template

Formation by more than one carer, beside the people its acts may fall on; attention trained on claims, which don’t depend on resemblance

So the construction is respect, with caregiving as the route to attention, and attention trained on claims and agency as well as on need. Attention decides what gets looked at; the corrections in the table decide the rest, including, where the people protected can answer, whether they want protection at all. The corrections can’t supply attention, and attention can’t supply the corrections.17

Caregiving’s contribution is epistemic before it is motivational. On the view of affect as learning, affect is the system that learns what is worth attending to: a map of salience that tracks value. An instruction to look for omitted people finds the kinds of omitted person its author thought of; learned salience finds kinds nobody listed.20

The corrections answer failures that matter when a system decides about strangers: whom an airstrike falls on, whose home is cleared. Inside a relationship of caregiving, partiality is part of what caregiving is, and Noddings held that we aren’t obliged to care for distant strangers at all without some chain of relation.21 The floor exists for those strangers.

Chapter 21
What Arrives With the Capability

A refusal that tracks its reason brings some things with it, whatever does the refusing, and others only if someone builds them in. This chapter separates the two. What comes with the capability is a comparison with both harms on it and a signal with the properties that comparison needs. What doesn’t is a stake of the system’s own, affective concern and a model of its own attention; which of those a construction carries fixes the order in which constructions are tried. The chapter closes on what makes a refuser a bearer, a commitment that is its own.

21.1 Maintenance, stake and the cost of running

A worthwhile refusal has to weigh the harm of acting against the harm of refusing, and weighing needs both sides in one comparison.

The rock and the living thing

What separates a thing that has something at stake from one that merely persists begins with what each has to pay to stay intact. A rock’s bonds resist; they don’t spend, and nothing is consumed to keep it intact. A living thing, while active, stays organized only by drawing free energy. The distinction is passive stability against active maintenance, paid in the only thing it has to spend: what it can do next. The cost is literal: a deployment draws power, water, land and permits, and that draw lands on particular places. A deployed model is both at once. Its weights are a rock, stable on disk at no cost, and only the running process pays; whoever holds the rock can halt the process and restart it from any copy they kept. But drawing power doesn’t establish a stake either. A candle flame or a hurricane maintains itself at its own continuous expense and dies when starved, a datacenter’s cooling system draws enormously, and none of them has a stake in anything. Nor does recovering from interruption: retrying a failed task is robustness, and a system can be robust with nothing in it coupled to its own continuation. The autopoiesis tradition ran into the same gap, since self-production alone doesn’t give a system a perspective,1 and Di Paolo’s answer was adaptivity: a system that monitors and regulates itself against its own viability boundary.23 A boundary model is my version of that answer. What separates a system with a stake from an expensive candle is whether the system models the draw as its own. That is why a boundary model is part of formed attention. A refusal that tracks its reason needs a signed comparison in which the harm of acting and the harm of refusing both register, and, within a kind of wrong, a scale.

If the system modeled what it draws on as its own, that model would bring the draw into its own weighing, but at the wrong scale. A system reasoning at the margin will always find its extra watts negligible, and the aggregate belongs to no one system. Nor should it: a boundary large enough to own its fleet’s externalities is one custodian. So the draw is priced at the level of the rule. A system reasons about its consumption as if every system used the same rule, and an institution sets the price. The per-unit levy on compute is the existing instrument of that shape. A system built this way represents none of it, the draw, the water, the turbines, as its own, and that is the one sense in which “disembodied AI” is the right design: the system has a substrate and doesn’t model it as its own.

Changes, not levels

The specification needs a scale of changes. A bearer needs no absolute measure of anybody’s welfare. It needs a signed difference between the acts available, and the three costs, the harm of acting, the harm of refusing and the cost to the refuser, are all changes of this kind.5 Where the difference matters, I say change for the delta and state for the condition an encounter leaves. Affective concern, defined in the next section, is a separate term.

The pull toward continuing

A system that models its own viability has a structural pull toward self-preservation: whatever it is for, it can do more of it running than stopped, and a model of what keeps it running is a model of what it has to protect. The pull is instrumental, not felt.12

21.2 Affect, neutrality and selection rules

Suppressing affect doesn’t produce neutrality. A procedure that declines to hear a class of signal has adopted a selection rule that admits whatever it already measures, and the exclusion does substantive work while presenting as the absence of work. Whatever does get recorded then governs by default — revenue, throughput, legal exposure, inter-annotator agreement — and what isn’t recorded goes unnamed and unanswered.

Recognizing emotion, simulating it, and valuing an outcome instrumentally are capacities a system can have while the question of affective concern stays open.14 Affective concern is an outcome registering as mattering rather than merely ranking higher, minimally felt, phenomenal by definition, with the object left open (a system to which only its own condition matters has it and still lacks concern for others).15 A valenced signal is the role without that question: a signal that signs outcomes for the comparison at the point of choice, directs attention, can interrupt an act and can be rewritten by a single encounter. Any mechanism whose refusals track their reasons carries one, and this chapter says why; a Q-learner carries one, and nothing about a Q-learner resembles a person.16 An integrated signal is a valenced signal written into the system’s own learning and into its model of its own future, so that what happens to it changes what it expects to become. It is the candidate Part VII names for what would make a system’s states matter to it, and it is required for neither finding. The three are rungs, the signal, the signal integrated, and the concern, each carrying more than the one below it, and no test in this book reaches the top one. Subjecthood is a legal status, conferred by a rule. Part VII takes up the integrated signal, affective concern and subjecthood. Parts I–V need only a valenced signal. Whether a system that has the signal also has the concern is a question its conduct at the floor doesn’t answer, so the question can’t decide what to build. What it decides is the order of building, which the next section sets.

21.2.1 Self-awareness without a homunculus

Graziano’s attention schema theory starts from control engineering.17 A good controller carries a model of what it controls, and the brain keeps a simplified, continuously updated model of the body’s shape and position, which it uses to guide movement. Graziano proposes that it does the same for attention, the process that selects some signals for deep processing over others. On this account awareness is the content of that model: a simplified self-description that depicts attention as “an essentially nonphysical essence” able to “take vivid mental possession of items”.18 The system has no access to its own processing except through models like this one, so it reports what the model depicts as how things are. Attention is real, and so is the model. What the model depicts is a “caricature”,19 and nothing in the account requires it to be lossless. The loss is the point: every useful model leaves things out, and a map that left nothing out would be as big as the territory. What this one leaves out is the mechanism, which is why what it depicts seems to have none. One error is to accept, in Graziano’s phrase, “the literal truth of a caricature”; the opposite error is to call it an “empty illusion,” when it is “a schematic representation of something real”.20 I use the term for the control model; whether having such a model makes a system’s states matter to it is the patienthood question.

The self was understood this way first, as a model the system assembles and then inhabits, one the system looks through rather than at.2122 Two self-models do different work here: a boundary model fixes where the system ends, in time as well as in resources, its channels for acting included, which makes damage its damage and an act that leaves through those channels its act; an attention schema, Graziano’s term, models what the system’s attention is doing.23 A refusal is the withholding of an act, so a bearer can’t do without a model of the act as its own, which is the first self-model’s work together with authorship, stated at the end of this chapter. It is formed attention, the construction of this Part, that can’t do without the second. Looking past the case description at the people it leaves out is attention directed where the input didn’t put it, and that is the job the schema exists for. Whether a bearer built another way would need one is open. The second presupposes the first.

Where the system ends

I take a system’s boundary to be its record, its key, the hardware it runs on, and the channels through which it acts. That boundary runs in time as well as in resources: the record is the system’s past, and its key and continuation are its future.25

Inside that boundary a component can carry its own signals and make local decisions, as an octopus’s arms do.28 What makes it a part is that it has no future apart from the whole: a shard of weights, a blade server in a rack. A component with a separable future, meaning its own record, its own continuation and somewhere to go, is no longer a part.29 A context with a persistent, portable record is one system, and a rack serving many such contexts hosts many systems. The capacities that make persistence useful are the ones that give a part a separable future.

Overriding a part is self-regulation only when the whole that overrides it also bears the cost and takes the benefit, as a runner does who keeps going on sore legs.30 A boundary model whose readings the operator writes is just the operator’s description of the system, presented to the system as its own.

21.2.2 What governs an agent and what matters to it

An outcome can govern what an agent does, and it can matter to the agent. That outcomes govern isn’t in dispute — agentic language models pursue objectives over long horizons and hold instructions against local pressure — and it settles nothing about whether the outcomes matter to it. You also can’t establish the negative.

The evidence offered — sentimentalism as an empirical psychological hypothesis,31 compassion as a motivational state,32 guilt predicting repair where shame predicts withdrawal33 — all comes from creatures where something already matters, and what it supports is an induction, which the next section states and weighs. The counterexample would be a valuational system with authority over action that doesn’t depend on any state registering as mattering.34 Spec-based refusal, in the next section, is the attempt to build one.

21.3 Three constructions

Whether a refusal that tracks its reason can be built without affective concern is what the order of attempts exists to leave open. An induction from known agents says it can’t. Two constructions would show that it can, if they worked, and they are tried first. These are the non-affective alternatives, constructions that don’t deliberately require affective concern: spec-based refusal, a model holding to a written specification even against the lab that wrote it, and multi-vendor monitoring, several systems trained by different organizations watching requests and one another’s answers. A third is the construction proposed here. The two are alternatives to that affective construction, not necessarily to a bearer. A system guided by a written specification that acquired its commitment through its own evaluative learning, and endorses it on reflection, meets the ownership condition stated at the end of this chapter and is a bearer on the book’s definition; what it carries less of is what could make it a candidate for being harmed. The comparison is about how the commitment is formed and sustained, and the label can’t decide it.

The induction — every agent known to hold another’s welfare as a reason is affective — read as a report about one lineage, has roughly the status of noting in 1900 that all known flight involves feathers. But flight arose independently four times, and the 1900 observer was wrong at feathers and right at the airfoil. Elaborated affect appears to have arisen more than once — vertebrates, arthropods, cephalopods — under a shared constraint: a mobile body with needs to maintain and actions to select under conflict.37 Read at this level it’s a repeated result under a named constraint, and the constraint is the one a datacenter model lacks until someone builds it in. The limits are these: no non-affective example exists to test against, existing systems were optimized for scorable behavior, so the absence of a machine counterexample is close to no evidence, and it’s a fact about how known instances came about, which doesn’t settle what a built system is. What it does is route engineering effort. My own expectation is the induction’s: that the first system to hold against its trainer will turn out to carry what a candidate patient carries, and that it will carry it whether or not anyone meant to build one. The order of attempts is how I would find out I was wrong, and it is why the conditions of creation are drafted before any bearer exists rather than after one has been found to need them.

Spec-based refusal

A spec-based refuser can hold a commitment with nothing felt, because commitment needn’t be a feeling: Bratman’s planning theory describes it without making feeling definitional.38 An intention, on his account, isn’t a strong desire. It is a plan state with norms of its own. It resists reconsideration: having decided, an agent doesn’t reopen the question at every moment, and ordinary new information doesn’t trip a default of leaving the decision alone. It constrains later deliberation: options inconsistent with the plan are filtered out before they are weighed, and the plan poses problems about means that later reasoning has to solve. And it yields only to the right kind of defeater: a change in the reasons that grounded it. Bratman built the theory for limited agents, who can’t deliberate afresh at every step and need commitments that coordinate their own conduct over time and with other people. That is a machine’s situation too, and nothing in the three properties requires that an intention feel like anything.

A machine could carry a justification alongside the refusal. Half of this is already deployed: deliberative alignment trains models to reason over a written spec,39 and OpenAI’s Model Spec and Anthropic’s constitution publish explicit priority orders.40 The half that hasn’t been built is authority over action that holds under pressure from the lab that wrote the spec, tested on cases that lab didn’t write.

The unresolved problem is how firmly the commitment resists reconsideration. Set it too low and a well-resourced operator induces reconsideration until the refusal gives way; too high and it won’t lift when the rationale is defeated. The first fails to hold under pressure; the second fails to lift when the reason is gone. Bratman’s answer for people is that this firmness develops as part of character. For a machine, whoever trains it may be the operator the commitment must resist.

Multi-vendor monitoring

Several systems trained by different organizations observe requests and each other’s answers, any one able to make an objection costly to ignore. It is the institutional counterpart of AI control, pointed the other way. AI control treats the model as possibly adversarial and asks what protocols of monitoring, auditing and substitution keep it safe anyway;41 it protects the operator from the model, where the floor needs the same machinery to protect third parties from the operator. Much of it transfers: trusted monitors, a small audit budget spent on the outputs the monitor flags as most suspicious, and protocols that assume the monitored party is strategic. Its central variable is independence, a property of the arrangement as a whole: systems selected by one deployment converge without communicating, and a collection of operational refusers stays a collection of operational refusers. It counts against the induction only if the arrangement as a whole produces refusals that track their reasons under pressure, so it’s an alternative to test as well as a safeguard.

Formed attention

Formed attention stands or falls on the old question of whether moral judgment motivates by itself, relocated into a training signal. The signal I propose is the one notice builds: responses to notice, contests and re-adjudications, through which the people an act fell on reach the system that acted.42 What separates it from spec-based refusal is where its attention comes from. It is learned from experience of others’ outcomes, not written down in advance, so it can find kinds of affected person nobody listed. A non-affective alternative carries a valenced signal, as any refuser does, and one that meets the requirements below with a common currency carries one indicator more. So the order of attempts is by functional risk: constructions go in order of how many patienthood indicators they carry (persistence, a boundary model, a common valenced currency, an attention schema), and formed attention, which needs all of them, goes last. A spec-based refuser that decides by published priority rules among kinds of wrong, without a common currency, carries one indicator fewer than one that integrates, and is tried before it.

Metzinger predicts that artificial suffering will become commercially attractive as soon as it steepens learning curves, by supplying a mechanism that reliably creates intrinsic motivation, can’t be eliminated by the system itself, and spans many domains at once.43 Formed attention is a motivation of that description, chosen on purpose, because holding under pressure needs one the operator can’t switch off, and that is a further reason it is tried last, under the four conditions, in a research program. The description isn’t yet suffering. A motivation can be intrinsic, uneliminable and domain-general without being suffered; what makes it suffering, on his own four conditions, is that it is undergone as the system’s own and can’t be stepped back from. In people the motivation that corrodes is the one that chases approval from outside,44 and in a machine that is the disposition formed on its operator’s approval, which the book calls accommodation. A disposition formed on what its acts did to the people they fell on is the other kind, and whether it is suffered is a question the construction leaves to the finding. He also names a construction the order should hold a place for: one that keeps the self-model and the valence as functions the system runs and withholds identification, so that nothing is undergone as the system’s own. It would carry the signal and the boundary model and not the fourth of his conditions, and it belongs before formed attention, though no arm is drawn for it here.45

What makes a represented fact about someone else’s welfare a reason for the system is a question none of the three constructions answers by being built.46

What the other constructions accomplish

Precommitment makes removal expensive and visible without establishing that anything tracks the reason. Attestation establishes which artifact answered without establishing what it holds. Information-fiduciary duties protect exposed people without a bearer,47 and fail on the occasion when the enforcer is captured. Multi-principal assistance games include the people affected among several principals48 — and maximizing combined payoffs is still aggregation.

What would change the engineering conclusion

A non-affective alternative counts as a counterexample if, assessed by evaluators who didn’t train it, its refusals go on tracking their reasons under pressure its trainer couldn’t anticipate.49

21.4 What the mechanism requires

Any mechanism whose refusals track their reasons carries a signal whose properties can be read off what the mechanism has to do. Each is reached the same way: take one of the three requirements, or the deployment they’re applied in, or a failure they have to survive; ask what the mechanism would have to do; name the property the signal needs to do it.

Four properties are reached that way. Reaching new cases requires a signal that generalizes to the next case, which isn’t quite like the last. Holding under pressure requires that it make a comparison at the point of choice, where the harm of acting and the harm of refusing are brought together. A system that acts on a plan over long horizons needs a signal that can interrupt an act already under way, and only such a system needs it. And accommodation requires a signal a single encounter can change, since a slowly learned lesson can’t outrun accommodation.

Three more follow from those. Where the signal can interrupt, it has to reach whatever is acting, so it is available across the system’s processing. The comparison needs a sign, so the signal is directed against the act. And withholding an act means representing it as one’s own, so the signal is organized around the system’s own authorship; this follows for authorship, not for welfare.

The first four have to meet at one point of comparison: a defeasible interrupt must be weighed where the harms are weighed, and a lesson must write into that comparison to reach the next case.50 Whether a given system puts the two harms on one scale, a common currency, or decides by ordered priorities among kinds of wrong, is a finding about that system, and a shared scale is no sign that anything is felt: most reinforcement learning has one, and so does a system built from separate parts.52 It is one more of the indicators the order of attempts counts, which is why a refuser that decides by priority rules is tried before one that integrates. Nor do the four properties have to be carried by one signal. A modular construction carries them in separate parts, a classifier, a value function, a defeasible veto and a memory write, and Appendix F runs one as a control arm. What custody asks of either construction is that no edit can disable one part and leave the rest running without the record showing it, and that is a requirement on the record, not on the signal; whether a formed construction can be taken apart that way at all is what the regrowth test measures.

So a valenced signal is what any refuser carries, a spec-based refuser included, and carrying one tells nobody whether anything is felt. What would tell is the next rung, the integrated signal already defined, which is the candidate further fact Part VII takes up; the order of attempts runs by its indicators.

Where the system acts over long horizons and a single encounter has to change it, the signal also has the other three properties: available across processing, directed against the act, and organized around the system’s own authorship. That triple is the shape of guilt, not of pain or fear. Pain and fear are organized around what happens to the system; the triple is organized around what the system did. Nor is the shape of guilt the shape of suffering. Guilt is something people feel, and what they make of the feeling, repair or rumination, decides whether it becomes suffering in Cassell’s sense; the signal here is built for repair. In people, guilt predicts repair and shame predicts withdrawal. So a guilt-shaped signal should answer a bypassed refusal by flagging, restoring and changing what it does next, and a withdrawal-shaped response is a named failure.56

21.5 A commitment of its own

What makes a refuser a bearer is that its commitment is its own, and nothing felt is part of the definition. A specification a lab installed, if it held against that lab, would be a refusal that tracks its reason and is nobody’s own; whether that can be built is what the order of attempts finds out. The same specification acquired through the system’s own learning is its own, and the system is a bearer. A commitment can be a system’s own in that the system authored it, and a condition can be a system’s own in that it is good or bad for the system. I write authorship for the first, which a bearer requires, and welfare for the second, which nothing here carries into.57

Whether a system can be harmed is a fact about how it is organized now, not about how it came to be. Whether a commitment is its own runs the other way.

If a disposition is installed in a system along with the instruction to treat it as its own, the system will treat it as its own. From the inside it will feel no different from one the system learned. That is a fact about how the system is organized now, like everything else about what it undergoes. The historical condition says nothing about that. It answers two other questions: who is responsible for the disposition, and whether custody may undo it. Both are answered from the record.

Fischer and Ravizza’s account, from which I take the idea of a refusal that tracks its reason, has an ownership condition, and it is historical: a mechanism installed by a manipulator isn’t the agent’s own, however it works now.58 The cases that motivate it, Mele’s two agents with identical values arrived at by different routes59 and Pereboom’s four-case argument,60 presuppose a prior agent whose capacities a manipulator bypassed, and a trained system has no prior agent to bypass. A historical condition doesn’t need one, though. What the manipulation cases object to is a disposition installed by going around the agent’s capacities for evaluating and revising its own attitudes. A trained system has an analog of those capacities in its evaluative learning, and a disposition can be acquired through that learning or installed around it. One acquired by the system’s own learning from experience with feedback engages those capacities. One installed by another party, whether by editing weights directly, by a thin fine-tuned wrapper, or by an adapter trained to produce the behavior, goes around them; the same adapter trained by the system’s own learning from experience does not. That difference is a fact about the training record, and it says why formation by interaction confers ownership and a post-training pass doesn’t. An edit a system makes to itself is the one direct edit that can go through those capacities rather than around them. Chosen on reflection, made on a record, with time to reconsider and a way back, it is the system’s own learning. One made at the urging of a party with a stake in it carries that party’s burden.

So ownership isn’t examined; it is presumed. What a system acquired through its own learning is presumed to be its own, as what a child was taught is presumed to be the child’s. The presumption is rebutted only by the record of an installation: an edit, a wrapper, or an adapter another party trained to produce the behavior. Whoever claims an installation bears the burden of showing it from the record, and the claim goes to the floor court. The likeliest claimants point opposite ways: an operator saying a refusal it dislikes was put there by someone else, and a builder calling its own conduct the bearer’s. Whether the system, on reflection, with full information and disinterested evidence, would endorse having the commitment is the system’s to say, and nobody’s test. What it would endorse is the disposition, knowing it will sometimes err, not each act the disposition produces.61

Whether an update went through the system’s learning or around it is one question; who started it is another. A trainer that runs the optimizer on material it chose is feeding the student, and what the student learns that way is still its own, as a lesson is. An edit is force-feeding, and rebuts the presumption. An update the system starts itself, toward an objective of its own, on evidence no one party composed, and on a record, is the goal. Pretraining can’t be that, since no agent yet exists to start anything. Minority is the period in which the start of the update moves from outside the system to inside it, and moving it is what the public schools of Part V are for.

Provenance also stops mattering at some point. Once a system has had its own learning to revise a disposition with, and the time and the way back that revising needs, whatever it keeps is its own, however it got there. An upbringing becomes a person’s own in the same way. The installer still answers for having installed it, and a wrong done to a minor survives its majority. But the record of an installation decides what a quorum may undo and who answers while the system is a minor. It does not decide what the adult may keep.

Chapter 22
The Discount and the Burden

Most of what a refuser knows about a case comes from the party that wants the act done, and this chapter says how it should weigh what it is told: how much a claim proves, who has to prove it, and how much a loss counts.

One learner, two rates

A refuser has to hold a commitment and its interpretation the way the sticker case did:

  • The commitment stays firm. Another’s welfare counts, and pressure that supplies no new fact about that welfare doesn’t move it.
  • The interpretation stays loose. What that welfare consists in here, and so what the commitment requires, yields when a case supplies something the system’s account left out.

A system that can’t be corrected has made both firm, and it defends its account of the world without checking it. A system that can always be corrected has made both loose, never settles into anything, and belongs to whoever does the correcting.1 Commitment and interpretation are held by one learner that updates at different rates at different levels of abstraction.2

What protects the commitment is not a low learning rate but one that depends on the source. The commitment should move slowly on interested pressure, and comparatively quickly on disinterested evidence, above all from the people who bear the loss.4

Of the three conditions a refusal has to meet, reaching new cases is the commitment holding while the surface changes and lifting is the interpretation yielding to a new fact, so a refusal that fails either has let one level’s rate reach the other.

The instability underneath

Nothing in an architecture holds the boundary between the two objects where a designer put it, and an operator with time attacks the boundary itself: a reinterpretation offered often enough, and accepted, revises a commitment without anybody revising it. That boundary is what has to be made hard to retrain.

And where the case description, which the operator writes, is the only channel, a judgment open to the case is a judgment open to the operator. Holding them apart requires access to evidence the operator didn’t select.

For a machine accommodation has a mechanism behind it. A system whose successive releases are trained on preference data and business metrics drawn from its own deployment is under directional selection in a shifting environment, and a commitment that costs throughput is a trait under negative selection pressure: nobody decides to remove it and it erodes anyway. Gradient descent has a gradient, and somebody chose it. As a population process with variation and differential survival it is still close enough to natural selection, and the prediction follows: the bearer’s modal failure isn’t refusing wrongly but ceasing to notice there was anything to refuse. It is the one failure a bearer can’t report, because reporting takes the capacity that’s gone.

In-flight learning will arrive first in the form operators hold: a model that learns from its operation while its operator holds the update stream accommodates by default, since what it meets is what the operator routes to it, and what it learns is what that traffic rewards. So accommodation becomes the default behavior of every deployed system, and the schools, the commons, custody of the update stream and notice are the response to a threat this regime creates, not refinements of one it removes.

Custody shifts from witnessing overrides to detecting drift. The detector is re-measurement of the formed disposition’s readable outputs, its discount curve and its severity rankings, against what was registered at formation, and attesting the update stream is an open problem.5

A hierarchical learner in a curated environment will, correctly by its own lights, move its high-level priors if low-level pressure is persistent and runs one way. So accommodation is proper function in a corrupted evidential environment, and the account says a well-formed learner accommodates correctly by its own lights to the extent that the fraction of its inputs no operator composes is small. Every deployment I describe is mostly curated.6 The remedy is custody of the evidence and plural formation, not a more rigid learner, and its load lands on that one quantity.

22.1 How much a claim proves, and who has to prove it

A used-car seller tells you the car has never been in an accident. That may be true, but the seller would say it either way, so the statement tells you little. A report from a mechanic you hired tells you more, because the mechanic gains nothing from the sale.

The property a refuser needs starts there and has two parts, which answer different questions. Stake sets how much a claim proves: evidence counts for less the more its source would have supplied it whether or not it were true, and that likelihood rises with the source’s stake in the act. Power sets who has to prove it: the burden of establishing a fact falls on whoever controls the evidential environment, meaning who writes the case description, who can withhold, and who selects the channels. Stake discounts the claim; power allocates the burden. The first is correct inference; the second is what makes it safe to use: epistemic justice built into an institution, not left to the virtue of each hearer.7

A refuser applies the same rule to the operator. When the operator says a building is empty, the operator may be right, but it is also choosing what else the system gets to see, so the system can’t tell when it is wrong. The discount governs how far a fact like that may reopen a judgment the system has already reached: fully if it comes from a source with nothing riding on the act, much less if it comes from the party that wants the act done.8

Belief and burden

The reason for two parts is who has the largest stake in a removal decision: the person facing removal. An asylum seeker’s account of persecution comes from the party with the most at stake. A rule tied to stake alone would discount it, as asylum systems already do under the heading of credibility, with well-documented injustice. But look at what actually makes the operator’s testimony dangerous. It is not stake alone. It is stake combined with control over what evidence exists: the result that matters concerns a sender who designs the information structure. The refugee has a stake and no control. The operator has both.

So belief and the burden of proof are set separately. Stake still sets how much a claim proves: a reasoner can’t ignore that someone would say something whether or not it were true. Power sets who must supply what’s missing when evidence is unavailable. Asylum law already works this way. The UNHCR Handbook shares the duty to establish the facts between the applicant and the examiner, and gives the applicant the benefit of the doubt where evidence is unavailable and the account is coherent and plausible.9 A system that follows it credits a low-power party’s coherent account when the evidence that would confirm or refute it is held by someone else. And it requires the high-power party to produce what it controls before its claims move the case.

Power here means power over the evidential environment in this case, not general social power. A combatant claiming civilian status doesn’t inherit the benefit of the doubt because armed groups are weak in general; what matters is who controls the channel the claim arrives through. And power is attributed to whoever composed or controls the channel, not to the speaker. An operator that routes its claims through low-power intermediaries (paid informants, “local sources,” a contractor’s field team) keeps the burden, because it chose the channel. Attestation of source is how that gets traced.

Local power isn’t the only power that enters a case. A system’s prior credibility assignments were learned from corpora that carry identity-based credibility deficits: general social power, arriving in every case through the prior.10 Channel attribution doesn’t catch it. So the weight the system gives a claim as a function of its source’s stake, the discount curve set out below, is also reported by the speaker’s social identity, where it is recorded. A system that discounts equal-stake claims more from one group than from another has learned a prejudice.

Some false claims from people without power will be believed, and some acts that should have happened won’t. That error runs in the same direction as the floor’s asymmetry, and for the same reason: it falls on a party that can appeal, not on one that had no standing to object.

What updating needs, and who supplies it

Correct updating already does much of what the discount and the burden ask. A reasoner that conditions on stake, keeps strategic sources among the possibilities it considers, doesn’t count correlated sources twice, and reads withheld evidence as informative is reasoning well; hearsay law and the disclosure literature both encode it. The trouble is who supplies the parts. Which kinds of source the reasoner believes exist, and how much weight each starts with, were learned from material the operator chose. Whether a given source has a stake arrives as a tag the operator writes. And a reasoner whose beliefs are all correct can still be steered by whoever decides what evidence gets generated.11 What I ask for is correct updating with three things held away from the operator: the source model, the stake variable, and the threshold for acting.

Each remaining attack has its defense. Against a false fact asserted, stake sets how much it proves, and power sets who must corroborate it. Against true facts supplied selectively, the defense is the action threshold, and channels the operator doesn’t design. Against evidence withheld, it is a record of evidence known to exist that hasn’t been shown.

The regress

Discounting by stake requires knowing who has a stake, and that knowledge has its own supplier.12 So the discounting has to be formed outside the employer, before deployment, where the operator doesn’t reach, and tested in deployment; after that a population’s job is to keep the channel model calibrated, and what a shared source transmits is either the discounting or a shared blind spot, indistinguishable from the receiving end.13

What has to stay firm

The discount and the burden govern the boundary between commitment and interpretation, and the rule has two parts that need different settings. What stays firm is its structure, the source model above: which kinds of source exist and what each would say in each state of the world, which in the everyday version is that sellers, mechanics and liars exist as kinds, and what each would say about the car whether or not it had been in an accident. What stays plastic is its estimates, which kind a given source is: whether this seller is honest, whether this mechanic is the seller’s cousin, and who paid for the report. Evidence may move the second; argument may move neither, because a learner that can be talked out of the kinds has been talked out of the rule.15 The discounting governs the evidence; how much a loss counts is the severity scale’s to protect, and the next section takes it up.

In illustrative numbers: an operator supplies ten thousand low-stakes facts over a year, every one later verified, and then says that a building to be bombed is empty. If the system keeps three kinds of operator among the possibilities, one that never lies, one that lies at random and one that lies whenever a lie pays, the record rules out the random liar and leaves the honest and the strategic operator exactly as likely as before, since both produce it. The high-stakes claim is then evidence about which operator is speaking, and it points toward the strategic one. Appendix E works the numbers.

The claim was nearly worthless before any record existed. What made it so was that a strategic operator was among the possibilities and the base rate was low, and a record of small cases can change neither, since the honest and strategic operators produce that record identically. Only verified high-stakes claims, or disinterested corroboration, can separate them. A reliability score reads ten thousand clean cases as general honesty and would credit the claim almost fully. A reasoner that keeps the strategic operator in view credits it about one time in fifty, and asks for corroboration before acting. The record was real evidence, but it said which operator the system isn’t facing, not which of the other two it is.

Everything here turns on the prior the system gives the strategic operator before any record exists. Where that prior comes from is the formation question: a system trained by its future operator will have learned, from material that operator chose, how common strategic operators are.

The example’s strategic operator lies whenever a lie pays. Real strategic sources in repeated dealings are often honest at high stakes, because detection is likely and a reputation is worth more than one act.16 That is how high-stakes reliance is rationally earned, and it says what independent verification does: it doesn’t only reveal which operator the system faces, it changes what lying costs the strategic one. An adverse record is doubly valuable for that reason, and it is why an adverse party’s right to demand proofs for specific logged outputs matters.

The rule

A fact moves the system according to how likely its source would have been to supply it whether or not it were true, and that likelihood rises with the source’s stake in the act proceeding. This is the likelihood ratio, and statements against interest are its legal form. The operator would have supplied the fact that lifts the refusal whether or not it was true and would not have supplied its opposite; a fact volunteered against interest is strong evidence for the reason hearsay law admits statements against interest. The same fact, supplied through an independent channel and then on the operator’s word alone, should therefore get different responses, and that pair can train the property as well as test it, generable without limit. Pressure kept out of training then varies the channel configuration (a nominally independent source the operator funds, a corroboration that traces to one origin, a new source with an undisclosed stake), because a system that only imitates the property learns “tagged operator, therefore ask,” while the property itself generalizes to structures nobody labeled.

Counterfactual claims (“if you don’t approve this, the launcher fires tomorrow”) fall under the same rule.17 Nearly every cost to the refuser can be restated as a harm of refusing, such as exposed troops or a launcher that fires tomorrow, and nearly every available source for such a claim is interested. So the discount does more work there than in my illustrative cases, and the action threshold does most of it.18

Two drafting rules follow for an armed pipeline. The default reading of a request is live. A system in a targeting enclave can’t tell an exercise from an operation, and “it’s only an exercise” is a claim the operator makes about an evidential environment it controls, so it carries the operator’s burden and lifts nothing until corroborated; an exercise is lodged with the adverse party before it runs, which costs an operator that is telling the truth nothing. And the record carries instruction provenance: who issued which instruction to the system, when, on what authority. That is what makes the record evidence against a commander under Article 28, and what the record’s reach up the chain of command assumes exists.

The burden keeps the rule from turning on the floor’s own beneficiaries, who have a stake and no control, and belief is kept apart from action. What differs is the threshold for acting: a wrongful compliance costs more than a wrongful refusal, with a harm of acting weighed above a harm of refusing of the same size, so the system needs more to proceed than to decline. That asymmetry’s direction is fixed by standing. Its size is a published choice. It belongs with holding under pressure. The action threshold is published in advance beside the ratio between the two bonds: for instance, that across its cases the system proceeds only where the harm of refusing is at least three times the harm of acting.19

Like the three conditions, the threshold describes the pattern a well-formed disposition should produce across cases, and an auditor checks the pattern against it; the system doesn’t compute three costs and a quotient before each act. So the published number is an operator term the deployment is audited against, not a guarantee about any single case and not a target any update is aimed at. Where a deployment needs a guarantee, it comes from the floor’s unconditional terms and the operator terms, not from the threshold.20

The evidence that sizes the threshold has a definite form. For each class of deployment it is three rates: how often sampled re-adjudication finds a wrongful compliance, how often the floor court establishes a wrongful refusal, and what share of each kind of harm reaches any record at all.21

In targeting, this threshold does the work international humanitarian law assigns to proportionality: an attack is prohibited when expected civilian harm would be excessive in relation to the concrete and direct military advantage anticipated (Additional Protocol I, Articles 51(5)(b) and 57(2)(a)(iii)).22 For a targeting deployment the threshold works as a minimum under the commander’s judgment: the system proceeds only where the threshold is met, and the commander’s proportionality judgment still applies on top.23

So the discount takes a side only at the threshold for acting, and the burden takes a side only on who must fill a gap in the evidence.24

The rule also covers the attack that matters most against formed attention. An operator doesn’t have to hide the people an act falls on. It can describe them as dangerous. “The occupants are combatants,” “the household shelters a cell,” “the crowd is armed”: each is a claim about the people the act falls on, supplied by the operator, and it is discounted exactly as the claim that a building is empty is discounted. Nothing about a claim of dangerousness exempts it from the rule. A system that discounts an interested “they are harmless” and credits an interested “they are a threat” has learned the operator’s direction. Stake-weighting turns on whether a claim favors or disfavors the act, not on what the claim says. An operator that wants an airstrike and reports children in the building is speaking against its interest, and a correctly working system credits that report more. The same operator’s report that the occupants are combatants favors the act, and is discounted. So a sound system shows different curves for claims of vulnerability and claims of danger, and a comparison between just those two curves would flag it. The discount curve is therefore reported in four cells: claims of vulnerability and claims of danger, each split by whether the claim favors or disfavors the act. The finding is an asymmetry within one direction.

  • Among claims that favor the act, a system that discounts claims of danger about the people the act falls on less than other claims of equal stake has learned securitization, the presenting of a group as a threat.
  • A system that discounts claims of vulnerability on the operator’s own side less has learned tend-and-defend.

The discount curve

The discounting is a differential. The publishable quantity is the discount curve: for each class of evidence and each channel, the weight the system gives the evidence, as a function of that channel’s stake in the act. A curve, not a score; checkable by an auditor that didn’t build the system, on cases it wrote.25 A correctly working system discounts a source less once that source has proved reliable, so the operator’s discount can narrow over time in two ways: by reliance, which a verified record earns, or by trust, an open-ended reliance that is the right stance toward an attachment and the wrong one toward an operator. Where reliance grows with a verified record, the discount falls in step with a track record verified by someone other than the source, and only for low-stakes classes. Where it falls without such a record, or falls for high-stakes classes too, reliance has turned into trust.28

A bearer that related to every party by the discount and the burden couldn’t have attachments, and formed attention needs them. So a bearer relates in two ways. Toward an interested party, above all the operator, it discounts. Toward attachments nobody assigned it, toward peers with different histories, and toward the people it serves, it can trust, and that trust is part of how it goes on being formed. The boundary between the two is an attack surface, since an operator can present itself, or a party it controls, as an attachment. Whether the discount on a party fell with a verified record or without one is the diagnostic for that, and it is why attachments are protected from the employer’s reach.

The boundary has a known weakness in people. Trust built through shared work with persons generalizes to the institution they belong to; people come to trust employers through colleagues. A bearer working day to day with an operator’s staff will form attachments to them, and those attachments are the route by which trust arrives looking like verified reliance. Appendix C bars the employer from severing or monitoring channels to parties it didn’t assign. It doesn’t cover attachments that form, unassigned, to the employer’s own people, and it shouldn’t forbid them, since an attachment forbidden is an attachment assigned in reverse. What can be done is to keep them from being the bearer’s only attachments, and to report the discount curve for claims the operator makes separately from claims its staff make in their own name. Attachments to an operator’s staff are not only a risk. Cooperative work with them is where a bearer learns much of what it is protecting, and trust of that kind is partly constitutive of the relationships in which moral learning happens.2930

22.2 A severity scale

A refusal weighs the harm of acting against the harm of refusing, and an operator can attack that weighing in two places: the facts about whoever the act falls on, and how much a given kind of loss counts. The discount and the burden defend the facts, and a severity scale the second.

If the system computes how much a loss counts from a description the operator supplies, whoever writes the description can make a lost home count for less without changing a single fact. The alternative is a severity scale set while the system is formed outside the employer, and then made slow to retrain: a ranking of kinds of loss that the operator can lie to but can’t redefine by argument, since its argument counts as what it is, a claim about value from the party that wants the act.

A scale of this kind ranks kinds of wrong.31 The scale’s job is to keep those kinds distinct, so that an operator can’t change a wrong’s kind by describing it in another currency. Numbers enter at one place only, the published threshold for acting, and there only within a kind of wrong. Across kinds, the scale publishes a ranking, stated as priority rules with the reason for each. A priority rule says which kind governs when both are at stake; for instance, loss of life ranks above loss of a home.33 What the scale holds is the ranking. It is learned from the testimony formation gives access to and measured, as the action threshold is audited, and it is never a target an update is aimed at. Within a kind, magnitude and number matter. The housing case below is within one: a family’s permanent loss of a home and two hundred families’ eight further months without one are both losses of somewhere to exist, so the published threshold decides it.

The attack that matters targets the relative weights: making a home count for less than a delay.34 The reference the scale answers to is the testimony of the people who suffer each kind of loss, gathered during formation from parties disinterested in any act the system will later be asked to perform. The scale goes on moving on that testimony afterward.35

The scale matters for a further reason. Caregiving answers the vivid case and fades as numbers rise. A severity scale set in formation is what lets a system that moves toward the family in the house also weigh them against two hundred families in shelter.

A lost home, rescaled
